name: Spatio-temporal deep models for conflict forecasting: Radford 2022 (ConvLSTM), Brandt et al. 2022 (ST-GCN), von der Maase 2025 (HydraNet, MC-dropout ConvLSTM U-Net), Iacus et al. 2025 (DynAttn, gated self-attention + ZINB); context from the ViEWS 2020 competition summary (Vesco et al. 2022) and the 2023/24 VIEWS challenge (Hegre et al. 2025)
type: method family (four papers: two peer-reviewed journal articles, two preprints/working papers) plus two peer-reviewed competition-summary papers used for context
url: Radford 2022: https://doi.org/10.1080/03050629.2022.2031182 (closed access; RePEc https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/ginixx/v48y2022i4p739-758.html) ; Brandt et al. 2022: https://doi.org/10.1080/03050629.2022.2036987 (open access CC BY-NC-ND; repository copy http://hdl.handle.net/10150/663780) ; von der Maase 2025: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14817 (code https://github.com/views-platform/views-hydranet) ; DynAttn: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.21435 ; context: Vesco et al. 2022 https://doi.org/10.1080/03050629.2022.2029856 (OA PDF via https://www.prio.org/publications/13337), Hegre et al. 2025 JPR https://doi.org/10.1177/00223433241300862
year: Radford 2022 (International Interactions 48(4):739-758, online 15 Mar 2022); Brandt et al. 2022 (International Interactions 48(4):800-822, online 14 Mar 2022); von der Maase 2025 (arXiv 2506.14817 v1, 8 Jun 2025, PRIO working paper dated 19 Jun 2025); Iacus et al. 2025 (arXiv 2512.21435 v1, 24 Dec 2025, only version as of 2026-10-17)
authors: Benjamin J. Radford (UNC Charlotte); Patrick T. Brandt, Vito D'Orazio, Latifur Khan, Yi-Fan Li, Javier Osorio, Marcus Sianan (UT Dallas / Arizona / WVU); Simon P. von der Maase (PRIO / VIEWS, sole author); Stefano M. Iacus, Haodong Qi, Marcello Carammia, Thomas Juneau (DynAttn)
popularity: Crossref citation counts retrieved 2026-10-17: Radford 2022 = 7; Brandt et al. 2022 = 20 (Semantic Scholar 18); Vesco et al. 2022 competition summary = 35. von der Maase 2025 and DynAttn 2025 are recent preprints with few or no citations [uncertain]. views-hydranet GitHub repo: 5 stars, MIT licence, last push 2026-10-16. No public DynAttn repo found.
peer_review_status: Radford 2022 and Brandt et al. 2022: peer-reviewed (International Interactions special issue on the ViEWS 2020 competition, with an external scoring committee). von der Maase 2025: preprint / PRIO working paper, not peer-reviewed; results partly benchmark against published ViEWS 2020 numbers rather than a re-run. DynAttn 2025: preprint, not peer-reviewed.
target_type: None of the four is a binary onset target in our sense. Radford and Brandt: continuous CHANGE target (log change in monthly state-based fatalities, ln(y_{t+s}+1) - ln(y_t+1)), i.e. an escalation/de-escalation target, scored by MSE/TADDA. HydraNet: multi-task - regression on log fatalities plus binary classification of 'any fatality' (>=1 death) per cell-month for three violence types; this binary label is a STATE-type indicator (violence present in month t+s), not 'new onset after peace', so persistent conflict cells inflate AUC/AP. DynAttn: COUNT target (monthly fatalities, ZINB) plus exceedance probabilities P(Y >= tau). The ViEWS organisers themselves note that the log(y+1) change target conflates onset and escalation.
target_definition: Radford 2022: log change in UCDP battle-related deaths (state-based) per PRIO-GRID cell-month, Africa, steps s = 2..7 months ahead (true future Oct 2020-Mar 2021 from data to Aug 2020; test 2017-2019). Brandt et al. 2022: same ViEWS 2020 competition target at pgm level; model predicts Q = 6 future steps from P = 54 past months. von der Maase 2025: cm = ln(fatalities+1) per type (sb/ns/os) at PRIO-GRID-month, plus binary any-violence per type; autoregressive forecasts up to 36 months ahead; metrics averaged over the 36-month test window. DynAttn: monthly fatality counts, horizons 1-12 months; exceedance thresholds tau = 25 (country) and tau = 1 (grid). All horizons are MONTHS; nothing below monthly resolution.
spatial_unit: PRIO-GRID cells (0.5 x 0.5 degree, ~55 km) over Africa (Radford, Brandt; HydraNet Africa + Middle East 180x180 grid, with ME excluded for the ViEWS comparison); DynAttn uses both 191 countries and 13,110 PRIO-GRID cells.
at_risk_masking: No. None of the papers excludes units already in conflict from training or scoring. HydraNet's binary 'any violence' task scores all cell-months, including cells with ongoing violence, which makes persistence highly predictive (state-target inflation). The change targets of Radford/Brandt implicitly condition on the current level via ln(y_t+1), but no explicit at-risk set is defined. DynAttn's exceedance probabilities are also unconditional on current state.
data_sources: UCDP-GED fatalities (via ViEWS / VIEWSER API), PRIO-GRID covariates. Radford: ViEWS 2020 competition data (training to Aug 2020; test 2017-2019; true future Oct 2020-Mar 2021). Brandt: 48 ViEWS pgm features (conflict history, protest, land use, socio-economic, resources, distance/accessibility) plus monthly ICEWS events aggregated to the 20 CAMEO root codes per cell-month (via UTD Event Data R package); train Jan 2000-Dec 2016, validation 2017, out-of-sample Jan 2018-Aug 2020. HydraNet: UCDP-GED only (sb/ns/os log fatalities, the ONLY inputs), 1990-2018 in partitions. DynAttn: VIEWS 'fast forward' competition dataset, UCDP monthly fatalities 1990-Jul 2025, several hundred covariates (conflict history and decay terms, climate indices, demographics, accessibility); test Aug 2024-Jul 2025.
data_source_variant: Not applicable (no Ukrainian air-raid alert data). Domain analogue: UCDP-GED 'final' vs 'candidate' releases (ViEWS 2020 competitors trained on the candidate dataset up to Aug 2020, later revised) is the conflict-data counterpart of official-vs-volunteer-vs-API variants; none of the papers quantifies the effect of revisions. ICEWS (Brandt) is a machine-coded news-event source with its own coverage drift.
preprocessing: Log(y+1) transform of fatality counts (all). Spatial rasterisation to a fixed PRIO-GRID; Brandt builds an undirected rook/queen-style adjacency graph of grid cells (A_ij = 1 for adjacent cells, plus self-loops). HydraNet: random spatial patch sampling (e.g. 32x32 cells through all months), curriculum learning, focal loss for classification and shrinkage loss for regression to fight zero-inflation (~0.5% positive cell-months). DynAttn: per-anchor standardisation using history up to the anchor only; missing values filled from the nearest previous observation (wording ambiguous) [uncertain]. No deduplication, gap masking or standing-event logic is described in any paper (events are monthly aggregates).
known_label_artefacts: Relevant artefacts reported or implied: (1) Extreme zero-inflation (~99.5% zeros at pgm; HydraNet AP random baseline ~0.005) makes 'exactly zero' and 'no-change' baselines very hard to beat on absolute-error metrics; Hegre et al. 2025 note the exactly-zero model is hard to beat at pgm. Analogous to our low hourly onset base rate. (2) The log(y+1) change target treats 0->10 deaths the same as 10->100 (Vesco et al. 2022), conflating onset with escalation - analogous to why we separate onset from state. (3) TADDA metric as parametrised in 2020 could not be beaten by no-change on the test set; the organisers changed the metric after the fact (TADDA1 vs TADDA2) - a metric-design artefact. (4) Single extreme events (Tigray Nov 2020-Feb 2021, >1,300 deaths in one month) dominate short true-future evaluation windows. (5) UCDP candidate vs final data revisions (not handled). None of these papers has duration-based artefacts (30-min ends, standing alerts, recording gaps, duplicate rows); for our project those remain governed by D-010, D-020, D-013 and the dedup-first rule.
model_family: Deep spatio-temporal neural networks: Radford - ConvLSTM (convolutional LSTM over the grid raster). Brandt - STGCN-TCN (3 stacked TCN-GCN-TCN 'sandwich' blocks, kernel 3, 1-hop graph conv per block => up to 3-hop spatial / ~5-month temporal receptive field, FC output head) and STGCN-LSTM; baseline is a random-forest regressor on ViEWS features. HydraNet - Monte Carlo Dropout LSTM U-Net (convolutional encoder-decoder with recurrent layers), multi-task (3 regression + 3 classification heads, Kendall uncertainty-weighted loss), autoregressive rollout with frozen cell state, 128 MC samples per forecast. DynAttn - shared softplus elastic-net feature gates + compact weight-tied self-attention encoder ([CLS] pooling, sinusoidal positions) + ZINB likelihood heads, ~0.88M parameters, rolling-window training with carried-forward optimizer state.
features: Radford: lagged fatality rasters (and possibly ViEWS covariates) [uncertain] (paper closed access); abstract states the model relies heavily on lagged fatality levels. Brandt: 48 ViEWS pgm features + 20 CAMEO root-code counts (d = 67 raw inputs), past 54 months, spatial neighbours via graph adjacency. HydraNet: ONLY the three log-fatality series (sb/ns/os) - no hand-crafted lags, decays or covariates; spatial and temporal structure learned by convolutions and recurrence. DynAttn: 104-123 predictors incl. conflict time-lags, exponential decay-of-violence terms at several half-lives (e.g. decay_ged_sb_100/500), spatial lags, climate indices (drought, temperature anomalies), demographics, accessibility. Common finding across all four: short-term own and neighbour violence history is the backbone; Brandt's backward-elimination ranks conflict-history features first, CAMEO events second; DynAttn's ablation shows decay and lag terms dominate (removing four such features raised MSE ~40% for Rwanda).
external_feature_timing: Brandt: ICEWS events and ViEWS covariates enter as same-month inputs within the 54-month input window up to the forecast origin; ICEWS publication lag and later revisions are not discussed, and ICEWS was later discontinued, so the feature is not reproducible in real time [uncertain] (on their exact lagging). HydraNet: no external features (fully endogenous). DynAttn: predictors stated to be lagged so that forecasts use only information available at t; climate indices are observed, not forecast, values; covariate release lags are not discussed [uncertain]. Radford: not verifiable (closed access).
ablation_design: Brandt: same-sample comparison of RF vs STGCN-LSTM vs STGCN-TCN, each with ViEWS features only (v) vs ViEWS + ICEWS (v+u), on the same Jan 2018-Aug 2020 rolling window; plus backward-elimination of six feature groups (retrain, average MSE over steps 1-6). Model and feature rankings flip between MSE and CRPS. HydraNet: no feature ablation (single input set); 12 training seeds, the run closest to the mean reported. DynAttn: feature-group ablations and elasticities per conflict system on the same rolling setup; baseline comparisons use different valid-prediction counts in some cells (e.g. 106 vs 191 countries), so not all comparisons are same-sample.
split_scheme: Radford/ViEWS 2020: two tasks - (1) one-shot TRUE future Oct 2020-Mar 2021 (forecasts made from data to Aug 2020, submitted before outcomes existed), (2) time-shifted test set Jan 2017-Dec 2019. Brandt: train 2000-2016, early-stopping validation 2017, rolling 6-month forecasts over Jan 2018-Aug 2020 using the previous 54 months, plus submitted true-future forecasts. HydraNet: ViEWS-style partitions - calibration (train 1990-2012, test 2013-2015) for hyperparameter tuning; validation (train 1990-2015, test 2016-2018) for the reported numbers; model retrained from scratch on the validation partition with frozen hyperparameters (no tuning on the final test). DynAttn: rolling monthly anchors (expanding window, optional cap on most recent K windows), test Aug 2024-Jul 2025.
metrics: Radford/Brandt (ViEWS 2020): MSE on log change, TADDA1/TADDA2 (direction-augmented absolute error), pEMDiv (earth mover's divergence for spatial patterns), MAL (model ablation loss in the ensemble); Brandt adds CRPS. HydraNet: MSE (regression); AUC, Average Precision (primary, chosen to match ViEWS), Brier score (classification); CRPS deferred to a 'future revision'. DynAttn: R^2 and RMSE per horizon; exceedance probabilities produced but not scored with Brier/log-loss or reliability diagrams [uncertain] (only partially read).
unit_of_metric: Pooled over all cell-months (or country-months) in every paper; no within-unit averaged AUC/AP. HydraNet averages metrics over the 36 test months (pooled over cells within each month).
baseline_strength: Mixed and mostly weak. ViEWS 2020: benchmark (ViEWS RF) and a no-change model; per Vesco et al. 2022 no submitted model beat no-change on TADDA on the 2017-2019 test set, at least one pgm model beat it on the true future at s = 2; Radford was runner-up on pgm MSE (avg 0.031 vs winner D'Orazio & Lin AutoML 0.025) and among the best on pEMDiv; Brandt's ST-GCN was more 'diverse' (useful in the ensemble) but not top on MSE. Brandt's own paper compares only to an RF regressor: step-1 MSE 2.86e-2 (RF, ViEWS features) vs 2.49e-2 (STGCN-TCN + ICEWS), ~13% lower; step-6 3.00e-2 vs 2.30e-2, ~23% lower (parsed from Table 2 [uncertain] (on exact parsing)); no no-change baseline. HydraNet: compares to no-change and to published ViEWS 2020 ensemble numbers - beats ViEWS on AP (sb 0.304 vs 0.272; ns 0.134 vs 0.047; os 0.162 vs 0.138) but LOSES on Brier to ViEWS for all three types (sb 0.009 vs 0.005; ns 0.004 vs 0.002; os 0.007 vs 0.003) and even to the no-change baseline on Brier for sb (0.009 vs 0.007) and os (0.007 vs 0.006); AUC mixed (sb 0.907 vs 0.921, ns 0.929 vs 0.894, os 0.884 vs 0.900). DynAttn: reports large gains (grid avg R^2 0.576 vs Prophet 0.248 vs VIEWS baseline 0.169), but LSTM, DynENet and PatchTST score near-zero R^2 and some 'Inf' RMSE - signs of under-tuned or failing deep baselines rather than a strong comparison. No paper uses a rolling recent-rate or calibrated-persistence baseline as in our D-021.
calibration: No reliability diagrams in any of the four. HydraNet claims 'calibrated uncertainty' via MC dropout but evaluates only point estimates (mean of 128 samples) and its Brier score is worse than both ViEWS and no-change for two of three violence types - consistent with focal loss (optimised for AP/hard examples) distorting probability calibration. DynAttn derives exceedance probabilities analytically from the ZINB head and presents them as calibrated without a formal calibration test [uncertain]. Brandt uses CRPS (a proper score sensitive to calibration) only for model ranking. Radford: point forecasts only.
calibration_under_drift: Not tested as calibration-in-the-large in any paper. Evidence of drift: ViEWS 2020 benchmark degraded substantially from the 2017-2019 test set to the true future; Tigray escalation dominated the true-future errors; HydraNet AP for sb decays from ~0.6 to <0.25 over the 36-month horizon; Hegre et al. 2025 note 2021 (Ethiopia, Ukraine) broke the exactly-zero baseline's CRPS. No recalibration method is applied; DynAttn's rolling monthly re-anchoring is the only adaptive mechanism.
uncertainty_of_gain: Vesco et al. 2022 bootstrap (1,000 resamples of predicted/observed pairs, i.i.d., not block) the MSE difference to the best model: at cm many intervals cross zero; at pgm Radford, Lindholm et al. and the ensemble are closest to the winner. Brandt, HydraNet and DynAttn report no CI or DM test on skill differences; HydraNet reports a single representative seed out of 12 (variability described as negligible after curriculum learning).
regime_coverage: Not applicable to UA alert regimes (Jan-2025 drone surge, Dec-2025 raion reform, Sep-2026 yellow/red). Domain regime shifts covered: ViEWS 2020 true future includes the Tigray war onset (Nov 2020); DynAttn's Aug 2024-Jul 2025 test spans ongoing Sudan/Sahel/Ukraine wars at country level; HydraNet's 2016-2018 test is a comparatively stable period.
leakage_handling: Done: ViEWS-style partitions with hyperparameters tuned on an earlier calibration partition and final scoring on a later partition (HydraNet), a fully prospective true-future task (ViEWS 2020: Radford, Brandt), early stopping on a separate 2017 validation year (Brandt), per-anchor standardisation using only past data and lagged predictors (DynAttn). Risks/missed: (1) HydraNet's 'out-of-sample' phase lets the recurrent network read the full partition volume including the hold-out months to update hidden/cell states before switching to autoregression [uncertain] (the text says it is exposed to the full data volume including test months, then predicts autoregressively from the end of training; this needs code inspection to confirm no test-month inputs reach the forecasts). (2) Brandt's TCN pads zeros on both ends and aggregates t-2..t+2 within the 54-month input window - non-causal (centered) inside the window; harmless only if the window ends at the forecast origin, which a truncation test would confirm [uncertain]. (3) ICEWS/UCDP candidate-data revisions are not reconstructed as of forecast date (vintage leakage). (4) DynAttn's imputation wording ('back filling from the nearest previous non-missing value') is ambiguous between forward- and backward-fill [uncertain]. (5) HydraNet compares against ViEWS numbers copied from Hegre et al. 2021a rather than re-running both under one evaluation script. No paper reports a truncation/negative-control leakage test.
test_window_hygiene: ViEWS 2020 competition is the cleanest: true-future forecasts submitted before outcomes existed, scored by an independent committee; but the committee changed the TADDA metric post hoc after reviewers' comments. HydraNet: tuning on the calibration partition, one final scoring on the validation partition, 12 seeds with the mean-closest one reported (reasonable); but the paper is a working paper whose CRPS evaluation is deferred, and the binary metric (AP) was chosen as primary because it was ViEWS' historical convention. Brandt: model selected on MSE over the same 2018-2020 window that is reported (selection and reporting on the same window) [uncertain]. DynAttn: single 12-month test; no pre-registration; baseline tuning not described. No pre-registration in any paper.
headline_results: Radford 2022: ConvLSTM beat the ViEWS benchmark and matched the best competition entries at pgm (runner-up on true-future MSE, avg 0.031 vs winner 0.025); relied heavily on lagged fatality levels to forecast decreases; underpredicted the magnitude of escalations and overpredicted their spatial spread. Brandt et al. 2022: ST-GCN improved MSE over an RF benchmark by roughly 13-23% across steps 1-6 (Table 2, parsed [uncertain]); STGCN-TCN trained in ~45 min vs ~9 h for STGCN-LSTM; CAMEO event data helped in some configurations and hurt in others; MSE- and CRPS-based model rankings disagreed (abstract: no single model dominates). von der Maase 2025 (HydraNet): with only three lagged-fatality inputs, beat the ViEWS 2020 ensemble on Average Precision for all three violence types (sb 0.304 vs 0.272), but had WORSE Brier than ViEWS for all three and worse Brier than no-change for sb and os; AUC split 1-2 against ViEWS. DynAttn 2025: lowest RMSE at most horizons and grid avg R^2 0.576 vs 0.169 for the VIEWS baseline, with largest gains at sparse grid level; short-term violence history is the main predictor, climate a conditional amplifier; competing deep baselines (LSTM, PatchTST, DynENet) near-zero R^2 or diverging. Context: across the ViEWS 2020 and 2023/24 challenges, most models (including sophisticated ML) were beaten by a no-change model on common metrics (Hegre et al. 2025), and the main gain came from an ensemble of diverse models (Vesco et al. 2022). Net: deep spatio-temporal models give small, metric-dependent gains over strong simple baselines, and gains on ranking metrics (AP/AUC) can coexist with losses on the proper score (Brier).
code_available: HydraNet: yes - https://github.com/views-platform/views-hydranet (MIT, active, 5 stars) plus views-models, views-pipeline-core, views-evaluation. Brandt: replication materials stated to be on the International Interactions Harvard Dataverse (http://dvn.iq.harvard.edu/dvn/dv/internationalinteractions); paper open access CC BY-NC-ND. Radford: competition required code submission to ViEWS; no public repository found; paper closed access [uncertain]. DynAttn: no code link on arXiv and no repository found (searched 2026-10-17) [uncertain].
takeaways_for_project: 1) Supports 'simple + correct' (CLAUDE.md goal): in the field's own benchmark competitions, deep spatio-temporal models produced only small, metric-dependent gains and most models lost to no-change on some metrics. Do not add a ConvLSTM/GNN/attention model; it would need a new dependency and human approval, and the evidence does not justify it at 24 units x hourly. 2) The learned signal in all four papers is short-term own and neighbour history - exactly our D-017/feature list (minutes_since_last_start, onsets_last_24h/7d, neighbors_active_at_t, national_active_count_at_t). Brandt's 1-hop graph convolution is a learned version of our hand-coded symmetric border table in src/regions.py; with 24 nodes a GBM on neighbour aggregates captures the same structure. 3) HydraNet is the key warning for our metric choice: it 'wins' on AP but loses on Brier, even to no-change. Our primary metric is Brier skill vs the rolling recent-rate baseline (D-021), with PR-AUC/AUC secondary - keep that order, and do not tune on AP or use focal loss/class reweighting, which distorts probabilities and would hurt BSS and the required reliability plot (D-006). 4) Baseline discipline: Brandt compares only to RF, DynAttn's deep baselines are broken (near-zero R^2, Inf RMSE) - weak baselines inflate gains. Our required baselines (climatology, rolling recent rate, raw and calibrated persistence; D-021) are stronger than any used here; report honestly if the model does not beat recent rate. 5) Target design: HydraNet's binary 'any violence in month' is a state target, and the ViEWS log-change target conflates onset with escalation. Our onset target with the at-risk mask (rows under alert at t excluded; asserted by a test) avoids both inflations. 6) Same-script evaluation: HydraNet copies ViEWS numbers from an earlier paper; we score model and all baselines together in one run, once, at the end of M4 (D-021/CLAUDE.md test rule). 7) Proper scoring and metric choice change rankings (Brandt MSE vs CRPS; ViEWS TADDA changed post hoc): fix metrics before looking at the test (already done in CLAUDE.md), and never change them after seeing results. 8) Regime drift is large in conflict data (benchmark collapsed on the true future; AP decays with horizon); our D-015 new-regime check with calibration-in-the-large is the right analogue, and a failed transfer should be reported as such. 9) Ensembling diverse simple models helped most in ViEWS 2020; if time allows, averaging the model with the recent-rate baseline is a cheap, explainable variant - but only as an extra row with human approval, not a new milestone.
best_practices: Adopt: prospective/true-future scoring and an independent, pre-fixed evaluation (ViEWS 2020); separate tuning partition from final-scoring partition and retrain with frozen hyperparameters (HydraNet; matches our train/val/test with no refit on train+val per D-021); report several seeds and pick a representative run, not the best; per-anchor standardisation and lagged predictors only (DynAttn; matches 'scalers fit on train only'); exponential decay-of-violence terms at several half-lives as features (DynAttn/ViEWS) - cheap and causal; ablate feature groups on the same sample (Brandt backward elimination); bootstrap CIs on skill differences (Vesco; we should use week-block, not i.i.d., bootstrap per D-013); report forecast degradation by horizon. Avoid: ranking-only headline metrics (AP/AUC) without a proper score; focal loss or reweighting when probabilities are the product; benchmarking against numbers copied from another paper instead of re-running baselines in the same pipeline; weak or broken baselines (RF-only, under-tuned LSTMs); state-type binary targets without an at-risk mask; changing the metric after seeing results; non-causal (centered/zero-padded) temporal convolutions unless a truncation test proves no leakage across the forecast origin; unacknowledged data vintages/revisions; claiming 'calibrated uncertainty' from MC dropout or a likelihood form without a reliability diagram.
